name: Anonymous lawn-care business
description: A lawn care / property maintenance business started straight out of high school in a small tourist town. About 90 recurring clients, mostly absentee holiday-home owners. Company structure, GST-registered (self-reported). The currency isn't stated; GST and "uni" suggest NZ or Australia (my read).

mentions.evidence: Last financial year (to March 2026): ~$57k revenue, ~$37k profit April–Sept 2026: ~$35k ex-GST ("mostly winter") · October "going to do over 15k this month" Buyer offered $30k for the client base + goodwill. The founder countered $35k upfront + up to $15k tied to six-month client retention.

sources.label: Reddit r/smallbusiness — "19, two years into my lawn care business, $30k offer on the table…" (15 Oct 2026, 226 points, 130 comments)

Sell it to Polish firms that look after holiday flats on the coast and in the mountains, and to the owners who live in Warsaw or abroad.

whyThisMatters:
A lawn care / property maintenance business started straight out of high school in a small tourist town. About 90 recurring clients, mostly absentee holiday-home owners. Company structure, GST-registered (self-reported). The currency isn't stated; GST and "uni" suggest NZ or Australia.

Absentee owners need someone to keep the place tidy, so they pay on a schedule and rarely churn. The owner is now selling the client list as an asset.

About ninety clients, mostly people who own a holiday house and do not live in it. He cuts the grass and keeps the place looked-after, on a schedule. The business is registered for GST. The currency is not named. The last winter was the busy half. A buyer offered a price for the client list, and he asked for more, with part of it tied to whether the clients stay. There is no company name and no site.
